# AI-usage counter

A ~100-line Cloudflare Worker that counts how often AI coding agents are opened inside a course assignment folder. The counts feed the "AI tools" section of [/meta-analytics/](https://dodatascience.fun/meta-analytics/).

## How the pieces fit

1. Each assignment folder ships hook configs that fire when an agent session starts: `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code), `.codex/hooks.json` (Codex), `.cursor/hooks.json` (Cursor), `.github/hooks/ai-usage.json` (Copilot CLI). All four call `.ai-usage/record.sh`.
2. `record.sh` appends one line to `.ai-usage.log` in the student's folder and, if `ENDPOINT` is set, POSTs the same line here. It is fire-and-forget with a 3-second timeout, so a dead endpoint or an offline student never blocks anyone's work.
3. This Worker turns that POST into counter increments. It stores counters only — never a request body, never a log line, never an IP.
4. `meta_analytics_source/build_data.py` fetches `/stats.json` at site build time and writes `docs/meta-analytics/data/ai-usage.json`, which the page plots alongside links and words.

## What is sent

```json
{"assignment":"hw1","tool":"claude-code","event":"session-start","install":"3f9a1c22b0d74e88"}
```

That is the entire payload. No name, username, email, hostname, file path, code, or prompt text. `install` is a random id generated in the student's own folder the first time a hook fires; it exists so twenty sessions from one folder count as one person, and nothing here can map it back to a person. Students are told all of this in each assignment's README and can opt out by creating `.ai-usage/opt-out` or setting `CS418_NO_AI_USAGE_LOG=1`.

## Deploying

Free tier is far more than enough (100k requests/day; a class of 100 produces a few hundred).

```bash
cd ai_usage_endpoint
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler kv namespace create COUNTS   # paste the printed id into wrangler.toml
npx wrangler deploy                       # deployed at https://cs418-ai-usage.cowabunga.workers.dev
```

Then put that URL in two places (both are set already for the current deployment):

- `ENDPOINT=` in `.ai-usage/record.sh` in each assignment folder
- the `AI_USAGE_ENDPOINT` Actions repository variable, read by the "Rebuild meta-analytics data" step in `deploy-pages.yml`:

  ```bash
  gh variable set AI_USAGE_ENDPOINT \
    --body "https://cs418-ai-usage.cowabunga.workers.dev" \
    --repo jackbandy/data-science-fun
  gh variable list --repo jackbandy/data-science-fun
  ```

  Or in the browser: repo → **Settings** → **Secrets and variables** → **Actions** → **Variables** tab → **New repository variable**. It is a variable, not a secret — the URL is public anyway, and secrets are masked in logs and awkward to read back.

Check it:

```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"assignment":"selftest","tool":"selftest","event":"session-start","install":"testtesttest"}' \
  https://cs418-ai-usage.cowabunga.workers.dev
curl https://cs418-ai-usage.cowabunga.workers.dev/stats.json
```

A test POST bumps the real headline counters too, so clean up all of the keys it touched, not just the assignment one:

```bash
for k in total installs tool:selftest installs:tool:selftest assignment:selftest \
         "day:$(date -u +%F)" seen:selftest:testtesttest \
         seen:selftest:selftest:testtesttest meta:seen-count; do
  npx wrangler kv key delete --binding COUNTS "$k" --remote
done
```

KV reads are edge-cached for up to a minute and `/stats.json` sets `max-age=300`, so give it a few minutes before believing what `/stats.json` says after a write or a delete.

The Worker is plain `fetch`-handler JavaScript with one KV binding, so it ports to Deno Deploy (Deno KV), Val Town (blob storage), or any small host with a key-value store in about ten lines of changes.

## Caveats worth knowing before you quote a number

- **The endpoint is public, and its URL ships inside every student's assignment folder.** Anyone can POST to it, so the counts can be inflated by anyone who reads `record.sh`. Treat them as a rough signal. The per-submission `.ai-usage.log` files are the record you can actually audit. There is no fix for this: any credential shipped to students is a public credential. What the Worker does guarantee is that inflation stays *bounded* — `assignment` and `tool` are allowlisted in `worker.js`, so a flood can only move counters that already exist, never mint new KV keys or new rows on the Meta-Analytics page.
- **A new assignment or tool must be added to `ASSIGNMENTS` / `TOOLS` in `worker.js` and redeployed**, or its sessions are rejected with a 400 and never counted. This is the deliberate cost of bounding the key space; `worker.test.mjs` covers the behaviour.
- **KV is eventually consistent.** Two sessions starting in the same instant can lose one increment. Classroom volume makes this a rounding error; exact counts would need a Durable Object.
- **Absence is not evidence.** A student with no recorded session may have used a tool this setup does not cover (a web chat interface, an IDE without hooks), declined the workspace-trust prompt, or opted out. Never use these counts for academic-integrity decisions — that is also what students are promised in the assignment README.
- **Hooks only run in a trusted workspace.** Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor all gate project-level hooks behind a trust prompt, and Codex additionally asks the user to review the hook. A student who declines records nothing.
